note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Extreme Value Policy Optimization (EVO): EVT-based extreme quantile constraint, extreme prioritization and importance resampling for zero-violation safe RL

nodes.name: Expectation constraints permit violations
nodes.description: Expectation-based constraints in CRL only guarantee compliance on average, so even when the expected cost satisfies the threshold, extreme tail events can cause frequent constraint violations (Fig 1a).

nodes.name: Existing probabilistic methods miss extremes
nodes.description: WCSAC approximates the cost distribution with a Gaussian that fails to capture tail behaviour, and QCPO's quantile constraint neglects the high variance and the exploitation of extreme samples.

nodes.name: Extreme samples are scarce and informative
nodes.description: Extreme reward samples reveal how to achieve task goals and extreme cost samples highlight critical constraints, but they are rare, making tail modelling high-variance.

nodes.name: EVT models tails with GPD
nodes.description: By the Pickands-type theorem, the conditional excess distribution above a high threshold converges to a Generalized Pareto distribution, so the cost tail can be modelled by a GPD (Theorem 3.1); a GPD fits better than a Gaussian (Fig 1b, Fig 7).

nodes.name: Quantile constraint formulation
nodes.description: Constraining the mu-quantile of the cumulative discounted cost, q_mu <= d, implies P(C <= d) >= mu.

nodes.name: Extreme quantile constraint
nodes.description: EVO fits a GPD to peaks C > q_mu and sets the risk boundary q_(mu+nu) = q_mu + GPD quantile, treating samples beyond it as extreme, giving an EVT-based optimization objective.

nodes.name: Extreme prioritization in replay
nodes.description: Each sample's replay priority p = omega_r + omega_c sums its quantile levels under the reward GPD and cost GPD, so lower-probability high-value samples are replayed more often.

nodes.name: Importance resampling reduces GPD variance
nodes.description: Reweighting stored off-policy samples by pi/pi_0 augments extreme samples and reduces the variance of the GPD fit.

nodes.name: Constraint violation upper bound
nodes.description: EVO's quantile objective gives an upper bound J_C(pi_k+1) <= d - (GPD quantile term) that is tighter than the expectation objective in CPO, guaranteeing strict constraint satisfaction at a zero-violation exploitation range nu_0 (Theorem 4.1).

nodes.name: Lower violation probability than expectation methods
nodes.description: When mu is set by the expected cumulative cost, EVO has a smaller constraint violation probability than the expectation-based objective (Theorem 4.2).

nodes.name: Lower variance than quantile regression
nodes.description: The EVO quantile estimator has variance negatively correlated with sample count and lower than quantile regression methods, so more extreme samples via resampling reduce variance (Theorem 4.3).

nodes.name: Zero violations on Safety Gymnasium
nodes.description: On Safety Gymnasium with infeasible initial policies, EVO converges rapidly to the feasible domain and maintains zero constraint violations while matching CPO's return and beating Saute and WCSAC (Fig 3).

nodes.name: Zero violations on Safety MuJoCo
nodes.description: On Safety MuJoCo tasks with feasible initial policies, EVO maintains zero violations throughout training, while WCSAC shows significant violations (Fig 4).

nodes.name: Ablation of EVT objective
nodes.description: Replacing the EVT-based objective with a constant quantile constraint achieves safety only by diminishing performance (Fig 5a,b).

nodes.name: Ablation of prioritization
nodes.description: Removing extreme prioritization degrades optimization, showing it exploits the learning signal in extreme samples (Fig 5).

nodes.name: Ablation of resampling
nodes.description: Removing off-policy importance resampling for GPD fitting worsens constraint satisfaction due to inaccurate tail modelling (Fig 6).

nodes.name: Sample-size sensitivity
nodes.description: Larger GPD fitting sample sizes generally improve constraint satisfaction, and EVO stays strong with as few as 10 samples in SafetyPointCircle1-v0 and above 20 in SafetyPointGoal1-v0 (Fig 8).

isolated_nodes.name: Experimental setup
isolated_nodes.description: Experiments run 10^7 steps with maximum trajectory length 1000 and 6 seeds on Safety Gymnasium and Safety MuJoCo, with cost threshold 25.

isolated_nodes.name: Prior EVT work does not address CRL
isolated_nodes.description: EVAC uses EVT to reduce variance in extreme returns but does not address constraint satisfaction in CRL.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from the failure of expectation/Gaussian constraints on tail events, through EVT/GPD tail modelling and the three EVO components, to theoretical guarantees and experimental validation.
